difficulty_reason: The lemma shows that for a locally finite type morphism and a generic point of the target, three conditions are equivalent: that all points of the fibre lie among the generic points of the source, that the morphism is quasi-finite at every point over that point, and that it is quasi-finite at the generic points of the source over that point. The proof derives the first two from the absence of specialisations in the fibre, notes the immediate implication, and closes the cycle by observing that generic points of the fibre are generic points of the source, so that quasi-finiteness there forces them to be closed in the fibre as well.
